text:
Sam T: Quick thread to capture follow-ups from yesterday's multi-region exercises. Two asks: billing attribution for failover, and auditability for residency-sensitive tenants.

Marta K: High level: finance wants predictability. Ops wants to bill actual consumed compute. Both valid. We need a documented policy and an automated reconciliation flow.

Omar B: Current infra tags costs by compute_zone at allocation. In a failover the allocation moves and the tag follows the runner. We can stop that, but it's a config change.

Sam T: Proposal sketch: introduce a per-tenant "billing_policy" enum: "home_region" | "served_region" | "reconciled_hybrid". Default = "home_region" for enterprise/residency tenants, default = "served_region" for self-serve.

Marta K: For hybrid, operational rule idea: attribute startup/cold costs to served_region for first X minutes or Y tokens, then switch to home_region. That keeps invoices sensible while covering cold-start spend.

Omar B: Technical bits: need header propagation from edge -> envoy -> sidecars -> collectors. Suggest header names: `X-Redwood-Home` and `X-Redwood-Served`. Also include `X-Redwood-Billing-Policy`.

Marta K: We must avoid header spoofing. Options: mTLS + signed header, or sign with ephemeral key. mTLS doesn't solve header injection at proxy layer. Prefer HMAC signer at edge with key stored in KMS.

Sam T: Agree. Example signature plan: edge signs with KMS-derived key, header `X-Redwood-Sig: v1:hexsig`. Downstream collectors validate signature against tenant_id and timestamp. Reject if missing/invalid.

Omar B: Implementation estimate: edge signing patch (1.5w), collector validation + log enrichment (1w), billing recon job (2w). Console and docs (0.5w). Can parallelize.

Marta K: Compliance request (Legal-Bot): need both served_region and home_region recorded per request for audits. Also require retention policy: default 12 months, but allow extensions for customers with longer needs. Legal-Bot: pinged.

Legal-Bot: Legal note: for customers with residency constraints, service terms may require us to keep detailed provenance for 3 years. Will confirm with counsel and post to the RFC.

Sam T: Edge cases: queued async work (background fan-outs) executed in different region — how attribute? Suggest tagging parent request id + region at time of enqueue and propagate on execution attempt. Billing recon job can aggregate.

Omar B: Also need to consider multi-model fanout where sub-requests go to different accelerators/hardware with different costs. Reconciliation job must accept many-to-one mapping.

Marta K: UX: Console needs a per-tenant toggle and an events timeline showing when served != home and why (failover, drain, manual override). That will reduce support escalations.

Sam T: Minimal actionable checklist for RFC follow-up: 1) header names and signing spec, 2) collector log schema (home/served/policy/sig), 3) billing recon algorithm doc + sample queries, 4) console surface + alerting, 5) retention and export controls for legal.

Omar B: I'll open a spike PR for header propagation with a small PoC in envoy filter. Will include unit tests for signature verification.

infra-bot: Created ticket #4921: "Add X-Redwood-* routing headers + edge signing" and assigned to Omar B.

Sam T: Thanks — assign owners in the RFC. I'll draft the follow-up and include the signature example below so implementers have a copy:
```
X-Redwood-Home: eu-1
X-Redwood-Served: us-3
X-Redwood-Billing-Policy: home_region
X-Redwood-Timestamp: 2026-03-22T15:12:03Z
X-Redwood-Sig: v1:8f3a9b... (HMAC-SHA256 of tenant|home|served|ts)
```
Marta K: One more: legacy tenants without a home set should default to `served_region` and we should surface a product task to collect residency metadata.

Sam T: Great. I'll post the RFC follow-up draft later today and tag owners: Omar -> edge work, Marta -> billing spec, Legal-Bot -> retention terms.

Marta K: :thumbsup:
